correctedFields.value: Strongest feature: The reply identifies the underdetermination between attaching classical attributes to divinity and specifying a discriminating hypothesis, challenging the inference from logical facts to a personal God. Principal limitation: It does not rebut every attributed property, while classical theism can present necessary, personal, and maximal characteristics whose evidential implications remain contestable. Live burden: The objection must identify the missing operational or comparative content, show how divine and impersonal alternatives accommodate the same evidence, and distinguish permissible metaphysical abstraction from evidentially disabling vagueness. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional terminological precision, proportionate argumentative force, direct engagement with the central burden, and a coherent discrimination challenge, moderated only by the limited property-specific rebuttal.

Strongest feature: The reply challenges both negative elimination and comparative warrant, explaining that the absence of an accepted natural account cannot independently provide likelihood evidence favoring supernatural causation. Principal limitation: Its near-exhaustive-candidate requirement remains insufficiently delimited, while the suggestion that good supernatural evidence may be unavailable overreaches the narrower, better-supported criticism of this abduction. Live burden: The skeptical case must specify sufficient comparative evidence, separate principled uncertainty from categorical exclusion, and identify credible candidate classes or predictive differences instead of relying upon unavailable data. Locked score: The strong band reflects substantial relevance, persuasive resistance to premature supernatural inference, and valuable attention to causal baselines, tempered by overbroad framing, inadequately justified universal requirements, and no complete positive alternative.
